blocks.content: Drumlins are inverted spoon-shaped or teardrop-shaped hills of till, often giving rise to what is known as a basket of eggs topography.

items: U-shaped valleys are formed by glacial erosion, whereas V-shaped valleys are produced by river erosion.
Do not confuse Eskers (sinuous ridges deposited by subglacial streams) with Drumlins (streamlined hills of unsorted till).
Roche Moutonnée features a gentle, smooth stoss side (abrasion) and a steep, jagged lee side (plucking), showing ice movement direction.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers erode land mainly through two processes: plucking (lifting of rock blocks) and abrasion (scratching and polishing by debris).
Cirques are deep, arm-chair-shaped depressions carved into mountain crests, which often hold Tarn lakes after the ice melts.
Hanging valleys are tributary valleys truncated high above the main U-shaped glacial trough, frequently giving rise to high waterfalls.
Moraines are unsorted glacial till deposits categorized as lateral, medial, ground, and terminal moraines based on position.
Drumlins are smooth, oval-shaped hills composed of till, oriented parallel to ice flow, creating a 'basket of eggs topography'.
